about:
# GSE: Advanced Macro Compiler
GSE is an advanced macro compiler for WoW.  Unlike WoW's macros, it doesn't get hung up on the success or failure of the current actions.  It just sends the commands to WoW and moves on to the next line.  This allows for creative approaches to overcome some of the limitations of WoW's macro system.  GSE cant break the rules, but it can make them more manageable. Every command available to WoW macros is available to GSE.

GSE uses the concept of a Block of commands.  For example you may want to target an enemy if you are not targeting one, cast a spell and use a trinket.  In GSE, you would arrange these as a stack and, at the click, send this stack to WoW to execute.  WoW will then work from the top of the stack down and attempt to execute each line.  As GSE follows all Blizzard's rules, it can only try One GCD ability in the stack, but as it moves on to the next block on the next click, you can try different things in case an ability is on cooldown, etc.

GSE started as a fork of Semlar's GnomeSequencer but has since undergone multiple rewrites and there now remains nothing of the original code.
 
# Features
- Loops
- In-game Editor
- Syntax Highlighting
- Macro Variables and WoW API incorporation
- Share Macro In-game
- Macro Debugger
- Macro Recorder
- Localisation support
- And more...

# Popular Destinations
- GSE Official - For issues with GSE - https://discord.com/invite/yUS9R4ZXZA
- GSE Tools - https://gse.tools 
- GSE United - For Sequences and help creating in GSE - https://discord.gg/gseunited
- GSE United Websites - For Sequences and help creating in GSE - https://gseunited.com
  
# More Information
- GSE Wiki: https://gse.tools/help

## [3.3.40](https://github.com/TimothyLuke/GSE-Advanced-Macro-Compiler/tree/3.3.40) (2026-11-23)
[Full Changelog](https://github.com/TimothyLuke/GSE-Advanced-Macro-Compiler/compare/3.3.39...3.3.40) [Previous Releases](https://github.com/TimothyLuke/GSE-Advanced-Macro-Compiler/releases)

- Merge pull request #2239 from LarryThiessen/macro-icon-black-background  
    #2238 Macro icon: a black background, so nothing shows through it on a button  
- Merge branch 'master' of https://github.com/TimothyLuke/GSE-Advanced-Macro-Compiler  
- #2236 Mor MoP Fixes  
- #2236 fix editor in MoP Classic  
- #2238 Macro icon: a black background, so nothing shows through it on a button  
    macro.png is the icon a macro step gets when it has none of its own  
    (Storage.lua), so it ends up on action buttons. Its art is round on a  
    see-through square, and on a bar with no slot art the world showed  
    through the corners. The same art now sits on opaque black, still  
    128 by 128. GSE's menu is black behind it already.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Merge pull request #2233 from LarryThiessen/action-bar-by-stance  
    #2232 Action Bar: sequences go on from the right-click menu, by stance  
- #2232 Specs: take the source from a match on, not the match alone  
    string.sub(assert(s:find(x, 1, true))) passes find's start and end on, so  
    the three specs searched only the matched line and failed in CI. Extra  
    parentheses keep the start alone. sequenceicon: unpack on Lua 5.4 too.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/master' into action-bar-by-stance  
- Merge pull request #2231 from LarryThiessen/bound-keys-at-once  
    #2230 Action Bar: a key bound or cleared in Key Bindings takes hold at once  
- #2232 Action Bar: sequences go on from the right-click menu, by stance  
    The action buttons' right-click menu is the one place a sequence goes on a  
    button: a Loadout submenu (ALL, or one saved talent loadout), a State  
    submenu of tick boxes on a button whose bar turns for a stance, form or  
    stealth, a Keybind row that opens WoW's Key Bindings at the button's  
    section, and the sequences. A tick on a button showing a sequence is saved  
    at once and put on the buttons when the menu closes. A stance changed  
    under the open menu rebuilds it for the new state inside the open menu.  
    A stance, form or stealth bar is a bar of its own: a Default row stays off  
    a page the bar turns to, in the button's click and in what GSE shows  
    (GSE.ButtonStancePages). Each State holds its own sequence; Clear Override  
    and a drag act on the state the button is in. A warrior's (Classic Era,  
    TBC, Forever) or monk's (MoP) Default rows are copied once onto each  
    stance they ran in. Only a form that brings up a bar on this client is a  
    State. The GSE Action Bar has no states, as before.  
    Bar addons: EllesmereUI's paging conditions are read off the bar;  
    DaylightUI's rule comes from its module, and a button running a sequence  
    gets its filled look; a row is re-filed onto the active bar addon's button  
    for the same home action slot, so a sequence stays on the bars through a  
    change of bar addon; an ElvUI bar's default state is its bar number;  
    Dominos gets its State choices and Button Forge buttons get the menu.  
    Editor: Button Bindings is out of the tree, and the Bindings area is left  
    out where GSE binds no keys itself. The page's own code is left as it is,  
    unreached.  
    Icon: a block's icon follows the stance, form or stealth across its lines,  
    Sprint ranks with the forms, and the icons are looked at again on  
    UPDATE\_STEALTH and UPDATE\_SHAPESHIFT\_FORM.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- #2230 Action Bar: a key bound or cleared in Key Bindings takes hold at once  
    With EllesmereUI, DaylightUI or Dominos, GSE routes a bar button's keys  
    through the button frame with priority override bindings on  
    GSE\_EABBindOwner. The routes were laid only while the overrides were  
    rebuilt, so a key bound in WoW's Key Bindings ran nothing, and a cleared  
    one went on running the sequence, until something else rebuilt them.  
    routeButtonKeys is now the one place a route is laid, and  
    rerouteButtonKeys lays them again the frame after UPDATE\_BINDINGS, out of  
    combat, only when a key has moved (laying a route fires UPDATE\_BINDINGS  
    itself). LoadOverrides clears both records where it clears the bindings.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- #2229 Button Bindings: key columns on the right, each row on one line  
    The row is now Action Bar Type, Sequence, State, Main Key, Backup Key.  
    Rows and headings no longer wrap: on a narrow pane the columns give  
    width back and the key text is cut to fit (the tooltip has every key).  
    NativeUI: flowNoWrap and a beforeLayout hook on containers.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- #2166 Action Bar: a bar turned off before 12.1.7 comes back hidden  
    When GSE turns the GSE Action Bar on to move keybinds, both bars start  
    hidden whenever GSE is the one turning it on, not only where the setting  
    was never set. A player who had switched the bar off no longer sees it  
    reappear on screen; a bar already on keeps its own visibility.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Merge pull request #2228 from LarryThiessen/profile-move-table-settings  
    #2227 Profiles: a table setting chosen before 3.3.39 survives the move  
- #2227 Profiles: a table setting chosen before 3.3.39 survives the move  
    The first read of a table setting (MacroResetModifiers, SkyRidingBinds)  
    copies the account's value into the current profile. On WoW Forever,  
    3.3.39 made that copy under the new class key, and mergeProfiles kept it  
    as the newer value: reset modifiers chosen on 3.3.38 came back as the  
    account default, and the profile they were saved under was removed.  
    A Settings table in the newer profile that still equals  
    GSEOptions.ProfileDefaults was never chosen there, so the older  
    profile's is taken. One changed since 3.3.39 is kept, as before.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- #2166 #2225 Profiles: kept by spec group, 1 Primary and 2 Secondary  
    Where binds are split by spec group (every client but Retail), a class's  
    profiles are now GSEStore.profile[classID][1] for Primary and [2] for  
    Secondary. They were kept by the class (9, and "9:2"), and on WoW  
    Forever until 3.3.39 by the one class-level specialisation the client  
    reports (Warlock 1490, "1490:2"). #2166 changed Forever's Primary from  
    1490 to 9 without moving what was saved, so every keybind, action bar  
    override and profile setting was lost on updating (#2225).  
    GSE.MoveProfilesToSpecGroups puts every class's profiles onto their spec  
    groups in one pass, once for the account (GSEOptions.Updates  
    .profileSpecGroups, from PerformOneOffEvents) -- the profiles are shared  
    by every character. On Forever it also reads the ids 3.3.38 saved under;  
    anything set up again since 3.3.39 wins, the older fills in the rest.  
    Each group is worked out before any is put back: a Paladin's Primary sat  
    at [2], where its Secondary goes.  
    Era, TBC, Wrath and MoP Classic profiles move from [class][class] to  
    [class][1] too. Retail keeps its profiles by specialisation.  
    Not yet tried in game.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- #2226 Action Bar Overrides: support DaylightUI's action bars  
    DaylightUI's bars are its own buttons (DaylightUIBar<1-8>Button<1-12>):  
    - hook the override menu onto them and list them in Button Bindings

## [3.3.39](https://github.com/TimothyLuke/GSE-Advanced-Macro-Compiler/tree/3.3.39) (2026-11-14)
[Full Changelog](https://github.com/TimothyLuke/GSE-Advanced-Macro-Compiler/compare/3.3.38...3.3.39) [Previous Releases](https://github.com/TimothyLuke/GSE-Advanced-Macro-Compiler/releases)

- Merge pull request #2221 from LarryThiessen/variable-save-status  
    #2220 Variables editor: Save reads "Saved", not "modified in other window"  
- #2220 Editor: variables and macros no longer borrow SequenceName  
    Variable pages wrote their name into editframe.SequenceName. A sequence  
    stays loaded while other pages are visited and only reloads when its  
    SequenceID changes, so going from sequence A to a variable and back  
    showed A under the variable's name -- and Save wrote it under that name.  
    Variable and macro pages now record what is open in ElementKind /  
    ElementName (SetOpenElement); sequence pages, a sequence load and the  
    editor's close clear it. The update handler matches by that:  
    - variable: by ElementName, as before, without touching SequenceName.  
    - macro: never matched. A macro writes every change as it is made, so  
      its updates come in bursts; the pending-save check says "Saved" for the  
      first and stays quiet for the rest. Before, a macro named like the last  
      sequence or variable opened (a variable and a macro both "Leader") read  
      "modified in other window" on every edit.  
    - sequence: by SequenceID / SequenceName, unchanged.  
    The minimised editor's title shows the open variable or macro first.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- #2220 Editor: a save under a new name clears its flag too  
    A rename comes back through the pending-save branch -- SequenceName still  
    holds the old name -- which read "Saved" but left editframe.save set.  
    Nothing cleared it after (deleting the old name sends no update), so the  
    next change another window made to what is open here read "Saved"  
    instead of "modified in other window". Renaming a sequence did the same.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- #2220 Variables editor: Save reads "Saved", not "modified in other window"  
    The variable editor sets the window's SequenceName to the variable's name,  
    so the VARIABLE\_UPDATED that its own Save sends back matched the  
    other-window branch: only the sequence Save set editframe.save. saveVariable  
    now sets it too.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Merge pull request #2219 from LarryThiessen/macro-length-letters  
    #2218 Macro length: count letters, as WoW's macro editor does, not bytes  
- Merge branch 'master' into macro-length-letters  
- #2215 Variables: the event choices no longer shadow the event list  
    luacheck failed the build: the dropdown's filtered table took the name  
    eventList, which the list of chosen events below already uses.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- #2218 Macro length: count letters, as WoW's macro editor does, not bytes  
    WoW's editor caps a macro at 255 letters (MacroFrameText letters="255",  
    GetNumLetters). GSE counted bytes, so a Cyrillic letter (two bytes in UTF-8)  
    counted twice: a 244-letter Russian macro showed 338 and could not be saved.  
    Count with WoW's strlenutf8, or a UTF-8 letter count outside the game.  
    Tested on Retail: a 188-letter, 298-byte block ran in full through the  
    button's macrotext.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- #2215 Variables: the event dropdown offers the common events, and only this client's  
    The Add Trigger Event list was missing events a variable commonly reacts  
    to -- UNIT\_INVENTORY\_CHANGED among them, which is how a weapon enchant  
    (imbue, poison) running out is noticed. Added: gear and bags, forms and  
    stealth, pet and totems, casting and channelling, movement and control,  
    focus, mouseover and nameplates, threat, power, stats, group and zone.  
    The list spans every client, so the editor now offers GSE's messages and  
    only the WoW events C\_EventUtils.IsEventValid accepts on the running  
    one; a client that cannot say gets the whole list. Any name can still  
    be typed in.  
    Fixes #2215  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- #2212 · Add Unit Tests for drag function  
- #2211 Editor: a spell nothing resolves is coloured unknown, not known  
    GetSpellId handed the typed name back as the answer in every mode but  
    ID when neither the client nor any locale's cache knew it, so the  
    editor (Current mode) coloured "Immolation" on a warlock who knows  
    Immolate -- or any typo -- as a known spell. It now returns nil in  
    every mode, and /cast keeps TranslateSpell's unknown colour instead of  
    writing the spell out plain.  
    Compiled macro text is unchanged (colour codes are stripped); a Spell  
    block still casts an unresolved name as typed.  
    Fixes #2211  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- #2166 Forever: Button Bindings arm at login, not after the first combat  
    On WoW Forever GetSpecializationInfo / GetNumSpecializations answer  
    nothing, and SpecIDForKey returned nil for the profile key instead of  
    Primary. With no profile, the login LoadOverrides armed no Blizzard or  
    ElvUI button; they only came alive when PLAYER\_REGEN\_ENABLED re-ran it.  
    Forever now never asks the spec API: Primary is the class and Secondary  
    class:2, as on TBC, Wrath and Era -- the key its saved profiles already  
    use. Elsewhere a nil answer early in a login still means Primary.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## [3.3.38](https://github.com/TimothyLuke/GSE-Advanced-Macro-Compiler/tree/3.3.38) (2026-11-08)
[Full Changelog](https://github.com/TimothyLuke/GSE-Advanced-Macro-Compiler/compare/3.3.37-a...3.3.38) [Previous Releases](https://github.com/TimothyLuke/GSE-Advanced-Macro-Compiler/releases)

- Merge pull request #2210 from Or1j1n/keep-toggle-guard-behind-conditionals  
    Translator: a clause keeps its ! guard behind conditionals and after a ;  
- Test the ! guard per clause: mixed, unknown, ranked and castsequence cases  
    Each clause keeps exactly the ! it was written with: none is carried to a  
    neighbouring clause, stripped, or doubled.  
- Merge pull request #2208 from LarryThiessen/drag-override-between-buttons  
    #2207 Action bar overrides: drag one to another button to move it  
- Keep the ! toggle guard behind conditionals and after a ;  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Spec: the drag test's game globals go on \_G, as busted needs  
    The drag spec set InCombatLockdown and the other game globals as plain  
    assignments. Under busted each spec file runs in its own environment, so  
    those went into the file's sandbox while the code read out of Events.lua  
    as text looked them up on the real globals and found nothing: six errors  
    in CI. They go on \_G now, as the teardown already restored them.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Stop tainting Blizzard's Options panel and action bars (#2206)  
    GSE replaced KeybindingsOverrides.AddBindingCategories to list the GSE  
    Action Bar's Key Bindings sections beside WoW's bars. Blizzard calls it  
    while building its Options panel at login, so the whole panel was built  
    tainted. Showing or hiding an action bar from Options then left the bars'  
    anchors tainted, and their layout was blocked in combat  
    (MainActionBar:SetPointBase()): the bars vanished until combat ended.  
    The replacement is gone; the sections sit where WoW puts them.  
    Adds TaintWatch (GSE/API/TaintWatch.lua, development builds only, inside  
    @debug@): records who taints Blizzard's bars and settings panel, with the  
    call stack, and /gsetaint scan lists Blizzard values an addon tainted.  
- GSE Action Bar: a button dragged off no longer keeps its gold ring  
    A CheckButton flips its checked state on every click. The press checked a  
    GSE Action Bar button, and the release that flips it back never comes once  
    a drag starts, so the button a sequence or action was dragged off kept its  
    checked ring. The drag start now unchecks it.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Action bar overrides: drag one to another button to move it  
    A sequence on an action button could be put there by a drag from the  
    editor, but once on a bar it could only be moved from the Button Bindings  
    page. The GSE Action Bar's own buttons already moved theirs by a drag.  
    Dragging an overridden button now picks its sequence up, as dragging an  
    action off a bar does: with the bars unlocked, or with the Lock Action Bars  
    key held. It uses the drag the GSE Action Bar has (BeginSequenceDrag,  
    MoveActionBarOverride): a drop on an empty button moves it, a drop on  
    another override swaps the two, a drop on nothing takes it off the bar.  
    Not in combat, not while the bar is swapped for a vehicle's, and not when  
    the drag picked something real up from the slot. A drag off a button plays  
    WoW's icon pick-up and drop sounds.  
    Taking an override off a Blizzard button also hid the button until a  
    reload where the bar always shows its buttons. BaseActionButtonMixin:  
    SetShowGrid adds a reason only when the button's grid is not showing yet,  
    so while GSE's showgrid bit was on, WoW never added its own; with GSE's  
    bit gone showgrid was 0. WoW's bit now goes on before GSE's comes off,  
    where the bar's Always Show Buttons setting asks for it.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

- Merge pull request #2205 from LarryThiessen/fix-numeric-bind-key  
    #2204 Keybinds: a key stored as a number is kept as its string  
- Keybinds: a key stored as a number is kept as its string  
    A user's Keybinds page (3.3.36) errored in loadRows, "attempt to compare  
    string with number": their spec's binds held [5] beside ["F"], and  
    table.sort cannot order the two. A number key also never bound (SetBinding  
    wants a string) and tripped the Action Bar's keybind migration the same way.  
    How the number got in is not known; nothing in the addon writes one.  
    GSE.RepairBindKeys (Profiles.lua), run by LoadKeyBindings before the  
    profile migration, moves every number key in this character's spec and  
    loadout binds and in every shared profile to its string, unless that string  
    is already bound.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- #2202 Fix error using an item based on range  
- Merge pull request #2201 from TimothyLuke/dependabot/npm\_and\_yarn/undici-6.29.1  
    Bump undici from 6.29.0 to 6.29.1  
- Merge pull request #2203 from LarryThiessen/fix-charge-cooldown  
    #2202 Action bar: a spell recharging a charge shows it on the button  
- Action bar: a spell recharging a charge shows it on the button  
    A spell with charges showed no cooldown on a GSE button while a charge  
    was recharging: with a charge left the spell's own cooldown is only the  
    global one, and the recharge, which a bar draws on the button's charge  
    frame, was never set. Measured on a Druid with a 2-charge, 120 s spell:  
    after one cast the spell cooldown was the 1 s global one and the charge  
    recharge 120 s.  
    The recharge now goes on the button's chargeCooldown frame, as  
    ActionButton\_ApplyCooldown draws it (the edge), and on the cooldown frame  
    too, as a cooldown with its swipe and number, so the time to the next  
    charge shows; the spell's own cooldown shows otherwise. On Retail the  
    recharge comes as a duration object (C\_Spell.GetSpellChargeDuration), so  
    secret values in combat pass to the frame; when the object cannot be read  
    as active, only the edge shows. Older clients read GetSpellCharges. For  
    overrides on WoW's bars and the GSE Action Bar alike; the bar's own  
    clears of the charge frame are put back as the cooldown frame's are, and  
    the frame is cleared when the override comes off or the button empties.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
    (cherry picked from commit 6cfb84b12df1450bcfca1e27a2f893aa65799202)  
- Bump undici from 6.29.0 to 6.29.1  
    Bumps [undici](https://github.com/nodejs/undici) from 6.29.0 to 6.29.1.  
    - [Release notes](https://github.com/nodejs/undici/releases)  
    - [Commits](https://github.com/nodejs/undici/compare/v6.29.0...v6.29.1)

      dependency-version: 6.29.1  
      dependency-type: indirect  
    ...
